reason: Response 2 goes deeper on leakage paths (session isolation, caches, refusals that confirm a document exists), but Response 1 covers the full harm set: hallucination, over-reliance, disclosure, chat logs and read-only agency, each with positive and negative controls, an honest statistical bound on zero-failure results and a narrower-launch fallback, and unlike Response 2 it sends employee-privacy, privilege and retention questions to counsel.
